episodes.title: Rethinking Civilization
episodes.description: Question traditional definitions of civilization and explore why some societies have chosen to live outside state control.

episodes.title: Money & Debt
episodes.description: Explore what money and debt do and how competing historical explanations connect them with trade, warfare, slavery, and states.

episodes.title: Disease!
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about one of his favorite topics, disease, as well as the effects that disease has had in human history.

episodes.title: War & Human Nature
episodes.description: Specifically, John talks about whether humanity is naturally warlike, hard-wired to kill, or if perhaps war is a cultural construct.

episodes.title: War and Civilization
episodes.description: In which John Green investigates war, and what exactly it may or may not be good for.

episodes.title: Climate Change, Chaos, and The Little Ice Age
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about the Little Ice Age.

episodes.title: Humans and Energy
episodes.description: In which Stan Muller subs for John Green and teaches you about energy and humanity.

episodes.title: Drought and Famine
episodes.description: Examine how disrupted food distribution turns drought into famine, using British India’s nineteenth-century famines as a case study.

episodes.title: How World War I Started
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about World War I and how it got started.

episodes.title: Who Started World War I
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you WHY World War I started.

episodes.title: The End of Civilization (In the Bronze Age)
episodes.description: Explore Bronze Age trade networks and alliances and competing explanations for their collapse across Egypt, the Levant, and Mesopotamia.

episodes.title: The Rise of the West and Historical Methodology
episodes.description: Compare historical explanations for Western dominance and consider how historians construct and evaluate those arguments.

episodes.title: Asian Responses to Imperialism
episodes.description: We'll look at the writings of Sayyid Jamal ad-Din al-Afghani from the Middle East, Liang Qichao from China, and Rabindranath Tagore from India.

episodes.title: The Railroad Journey and the Industrial Revolution
episodes.description: Explore how steam railways transformed travel, perceptions of time and space, and everyday habits during the Industrial Revolution.

episodes.title: Population, Sustainability, and Malthus
episodes.description: Examine Malthus’s population forecasts and how faulty assumptions can undermine predictions about human growth and resources.

episodes.title: Islam and Politics
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about how Islam has interacted with politics during its history, and how it continues to do so today.

episodes.title: The Mughal Empire and Historical Reputation
episodes.description: Examine the Mughal Empire and reassess the historical reputations of emperors Akbar and Aurangzeb.

episodes.title: Luther and the Protestant Reformation
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about the Protestant Reformation.

episodes.title: Charles V and the Holy Roman Empire
episodes.description: Explore Charles V’s overlapping titles and territories to understand the Holy Roman Empire and its wider connections.

episodes.title: World War II, A War for Resources
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about World War II, and some of the causes behind the war.

episodes.title: Congo and Africa’s World War
episodes.description: Trace the history of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the regional conflicts that involved Uganda, Rwanda, and neighboring countries.

episodes.title: Water and Classical Civilizations
episodes.description: Explore how access to water shaped the Maya and Khmer civilizations.

episodes.title: Conflict in Israel and Palestine
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about the conflict in Israel and Palestine.

episodes.title: The Vikings!
episodes.description: Explore Viking travel, trade, raiding, and Norse mythology beyond familiar stereotypes.

episodes.title: War and Nation Building in Latin America
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about nation building and nationalism in Latin America.

episodes.title: Iran’s Revolutions
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about Iran's Revolutions.

episodes.title: Japan in the Heian Period and Cultural History
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about what westerners call the middle ages and the lives of the aristocracy...in Japan.

episodes.title: Nonviolence and Peace Movements
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about nonviolence and peace movements in the 20th century.

episodes.title: Capitalism and the Dutch East India Company
episodes.description: In which John Green teaches you about the Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie, doing business as the VOC, also known as the Dutch East India Company.

episodes.title: Democracy, Authoritarian Capitalism, and China
episodes.description: Compare democratic and authoritarian forms of capitalism through the economic experiences of China and Singapore.
